source_repair.before_clause: **Pages:** spatial-point-process-summaries-and-palm-laws / spatial-point-process-summaries-and-palm-laws-examples. **A:** For a stationary point process $\eta$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite positive intensity $\rho$, define the second factorial moment measure $\alpha^{(2)}(A\times B)=E\sum_{x\ne y\in\eta}1_A(x)1_B(y)$, reduced moment measure, and pair-correlation density $g$ only when the required absolute-continuity density exists. Define the Palm law $P^0$ by the refined Campbell identity $E\sum_{x\in\eta}h(x,\eta-\delta_x)=\rho\int_{\mathbb R^d}E^0[h(x,\eta)]\,dx$, not by conditioning on a zero-probability event. Define Ripley's $K(r)=\rho^{-1}E^0[\eta(B(0,r)\setminus\{0\})]$; if the second factorial density is $\rho^2g(u)$, prove $K(r)=\int_{B(0,r)}g(u)\,du$, and for Poisson $K(r)=|B(0,r)|$. Define edge-corrected K estimators as procedures with the correction weight stated, with no automatic unbiasedness claim. For compact convex $W$ with nonempty interior and dilations $W_n=a_nW$, state the Last–Penrose result $\eta(W_n)/|W_n|\to E[\eta(Q)\mid\mathcal I]$ in $L^1$, where $Q$ is a unit-volume reference set and $\mathcal I$ is the translation-invariant sigma-algebra; ergodicity makes the limit $\rho$. No rate/CLT. **B:** edge effects and absent pair-correlation density. **Requires:** SME-48; published measure and ergodic suppliers under their exact conditions. **Sources:** Last–Penrose Ch.8 pp.81–93 Thm.8.14, Ch.9 pp.94–103 Thms.9.1/9.4; Baddeley Lectures 2–3 pp.26–56.
source_repair.after_clause: **Pages:** spatial-point-process-summaries-and-palm-laws / spatial-point-process-summaries-and-palm-laws-examples. **A:** For a stationary locally finite point process $\eta$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite positive intensity $\rho$, use the full Palm law $P^0$ and the recentering convention $(\theta_x\mu)(B)=\mu(B+x)$. Define $P^0$ by the refined Campbell identity $E\int h(x,\theta_x\eta)\,\eta(dx)=\rho\int_{\mathbb R^d}\int h(x,\mu)\,P^0(d\mu)\,dx$ for every nonnegative jointly measurable $h$, not by conditioning on a zero-probability event; this law retains the distinguished atom at the origin. If $\eta=\sum_i\delta_{X_i}$, define $\alpha^{(2)}(A\times B)=E\sum_{i\ne j}1_A(X_i)1_B(X_j)$, with distinct atom indices counting multiplicities; distinct locations suffice only for a simple process. On the locally square-integrable second-order route, define the reduced second factorial moment measure by $\alpha^{(2)}_{\rm red}(D)=E\sum_{i\ne j}1_Q(X_i)1_D(X_j-X_i)$ for the unit-volume cube $Q=[0,1)^d$, prove $\alpha^{(2)}_{\rm red}(D)=\rho\int(\mu-\delta_0)(D)\,P^0(d\mu)$, and define pair-correlation density $g$ only if $\alpha^{(2)}_{\rm red}(du)=\rho^2g(u)\,du$. For $r\ge0$, with the closed Euclidean ball convention, define Ripley's $K(r)=\rho^{-1}\int(\mu-\delta_0)(B(0,r))\,P^0(d\mu)=\rho^{-2}\alpha^{(2)}_{\rm red}(B(0,r))$; this removes one distinguished occurrence, retaining any other co-located atoms. For simple processes it equals $\rho^{-1}E^0[\mu(B(0,r)\setminus\{0\})]$. If $g$ exists, prove $K(r)=\int_{B(0,r)}g(u)\,du$; for homogeneous Poisson prove $K(r)=|B(0,r)|$ via the Mecke–Slivnyak full-Palm law $P^0=P(\eta+\delta_0\in\cdot)$. Define edge-corrected K estimators as procedures with the correction weight stated, with no automatic unbiasedness claim. For compact convex $W$ with nonempty interior and dilations $W_n=a_nW$, state the Last–Penrose result $\eta(W_n)/|W_n|\to E[\eta(Q)\mid\mathcal I]$ in $L^1$, where $Q$ is a unit-volume reference set and $\mathcal I$ is the translation-invariant sigma-algebra; ergodicity makes the limit $\rho$. No rate/CLT. **B:** edge effects, absent pair-correlation density, and a uniformly translated lattice showing why Palm configurations must be recentered; compare deletion of one occurrence with removal of all origin atoms when multiplicities are present. **Requires:** SME-48; published measure and ergodic suppliers under their exact conditions. **Sources:** Last–Penrose Ch.8 PDF pp.81–93 (printed pp.69–81), Def.8.6/Prop.8.7 and Thm.8.14; Ch.9 PDF pp.94–103 (printed pp.82–91), Thms.9.1/9.4, formula (9.6) and Exercise 9.9; Baddeley Lectures 2–3 pp.26–56.
